title: Reliability: timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, rate limiting, bulkheads, multi-region
summary: Designing for partial failure: timeouts and deadline budgets, retries with jitter and retry budgets, circuit breakers, rate limiting, bulkheads, load shedding, multi-region DR, correlated failures and chaos.

units.title: Isolation, degradation and surviving failure domains

labs.title: Retry executor: exponential backoff, full/equal/decorrelated jitter, deadline budget, Retry-After, idempotency gate, shared retry budget
Circuit breaker: rolling window, half-open probing, outcome classification, state-change callback
Rate limiters: token bucket, sliding-window log and counter, bounded per-key memory, Retry-After, 429 middleware
Bulkheads per dependency (bounded FIFO queue) and an AIMD adaptive concurrency limit

outcomes.text: Derive per-hop timeouts from a propagated deadline budget, order them across hops, and explain why a timeout is a capacity control as much as a correctness control.
Implement a retry executor with exponential backoff and full/equal/decorrelated jitter, Retry-After handling, a deadline budget, an idempotency gate and error classification.
Compute retry amplification, size a shared retry budget, and explain metastable failures and the defences against them.
Implement a circuit breaker with a rolling window, limited half-open probing and correct outcome classification, and design its fallback.

Choose between fixed-window, sliding-window (log and counter), token-bucket, leaky-bucket and GCRA limiters for a requirement, and implement token-bucket and sliding-window limiters with bounded memory and correct Retry-After.
Design rate limiting for a multi-node, multi-tenant API: local vs shared counters vs leases, fairness, fail-open vs fail-closed, 429 vs 503, and client behaviour.
Apply bulkheads, cells and shuffle sharding to contain failure, and size pools and queues with Little's law.
Design load shedding and graceful degradation for an overloaded service: priority classes, queue bounds, deadline-aware servers, brownouts.
Choose a multi-AZ / multi-region topology and DR tier from RPO, RTO and cost, and walk through a failover including fencing, split brain and the dependencies that quietly don't replicate.
Reason about availability with correlated failures, and design deploy-safety and chaos/game-day practices that exercise the failure paths.
Compose retry, breaker, bulkhead and limiter into one vendor adapter with an explicit error taxonomy, and predict how mis-ordering them fails.
Implement semaphore bulkheads per dependency and an AIMD adaptive concurrency limit, and explain hedged requests, GCRA and the leaky bucket as a shaper.
